scenes.say: Every Docker interview starts here. Do you know the real difference between an image and a container?

scenes.label: Image
scenes.sub: A read-only template, built in layers.
scenes.say: First up, an image is just a read-only template. Think of it as the blueprint for your app.

scenes.label: Container
scenes.sub: A running instance with its own writable layer.
scenes.say: A container is what you get when you launch that blueprint. It's running, and it has its own writable layer for changes.
If you know object-oriented programming, here's a shortcut: an image is like a class, while a container is like an object created from that class.

scenes.title: From image to container
scenes.say: You pull an image, list your images, and then run a container from it. Now, that container is alive and writable.

scenes.question: Is an image ever writable?
scenes.wrong: Yes, you can write to it.
scenes.right: Nope. Images are always read-only. Only containers get a writable layer on top.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: images are never writable. Only containers can be changed while running.
